pr_title: Switch order of zwave_js task cancelling on disconnect
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Sometimes when unloading the config entry, messages attempt to get sent after we disconnect from the server which raises an exception. As suggested in Discord (https://discord.com/channels/330944238910963714/800356888827002880/1184943010065158335) we are switching the order of operations to hopefully prevent this from occurring.

I don't know how to test this so open to suggestions

I am probably doing something incorrectly in the test but the following test passes on dev (commented out blocking because then it hangs indefinitely but I think because we are not blocking we aren't able to force the error):

```python
async def test_entry_unload_with_queued_command(hass: HomeAssistant, multisensor_6, client) -> None:
    """Test the integration unload succeeds even when there is a queued command."""
    event = asyncio.Event()

    async def hung_command(*_, **__):
        await event.wait()

    client.async_send_command.side_effect = hung_command

    entry = MockConfigEntry(domain="zwave_js", data={"url": "ws://test.org"})
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
    # await hass.async_block_till_done()

    await hass.config_entries.async_unload(entry.entry_id)

    assert client.disconnect.call_count == 1
    assert entry.state is ConfigEntryState.NOT_LOADED
```

also passing on dev and I still can't block, even if I create an `asyncio.Task` for the coroutine and await it after awaiting the unload:
```python
async def test_entry_unload_with_queued_command(hass: HomeAssistant, aeotec_zw164_siren_state, client) -> None:
    """Test the integration unload succeeds even when there is a queued command."""
    node_state = aeotec_zw164_siren_state
    wait_event = asyncio.Event()

    async def hung_command(*_, **__):
        await wait_event.wait()

    entry = MockConfigEntry(domain="zwave_js", data={"url": "ws://test.org"})
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    client.async_send_command.side_effect = hung_command

    # Add a node so we have a command to queue
    event = Event(
        type="node added",
        data={
            "source": "controller",
            "event": "node added",
            "node": node_state,
            "result": {},
        },
    )
    client.driver.receive_event(event)

    event = Event(
        type="ready",
        data={
            "source": "node",
            "event": "ready",
            "nodeId": node_state["nodeId"],
            "nodeState": node_state,
        },
    )
    client.driver.receive_event(event)

    await hass.config_entries.async_unload(entry.entry_id)
    # await hass.async_block_till_done()

    assert client.disconnect.call_count == 1
    assert entry.state is ConfigEntryState.NOT_LOADED
```

I've looked again at the flow and I don't think the flow is waiting in `Client.async_send_command` since then `Client._send_json_message` would already be called when we close the connection, which is not the case. The stacktrace raises `NotConnected` which means the connection is closed before the call to `Client._send_json_message`.

I think there's something else that takes a while or blocks until we start canceling tasks during config entry unload, and then the flow reaches `node.async_has_device_config_changed` which tries to send the command and blows up when the connection is closed. The only thing that we await in `async_on_node_ready` before the call to `node.async_has_device_config_changed` are the platform setups. So my guess right now is that some platform(s) is taking a while to setup and when we cancel the platform tasks the flow is released to call `node.async_has_device_config_changed` which then blows up when the connection is already closed.

I think we should cancel and await the start client task and the platform tasks before we cancel and await the listen task.

To test this, probably have some platform setup block on something. It would be best if we could find the platform that awaits something that can block for some time.
I tried using the diagnostics that the user provided to find the platform setup time but no dice. I wonder if Nick has tried profiling platform setups, I will reach out to him.

There are multiple error entries towards the end of the file that may indicate problems leading to the Z-Wave integration unloading. Here are some observations:

There is an error related to setting up a select entity within the Z-Wave JS integration​​.
Similar errors occurred while setting up number, light, and event entities, with all these errors pointing to the async_setup_entry function failing​​.
The error that directly precedes the unloading of the Z-Wave JS integration mentions the failure in an async_unload_entry function call​​.
Additionally, there is a debug message that a "No SPAN is established yet cannot decode command" error happened for Node 003, which could be related to security or communication issues with this particular Z-Wave node​​.

review_comments:
```suggestion
    # Cancel the start client task before cancelling the listen task
    # to allow client tasks to clean up before the connection to the server is closed
    # when the listen task is cancelled.
    start_client_task.cancel()
```

Is it possible for the connection to drop at any time during the start_client_task which would cause it to raise an exception?

If so it might be better to handle that case with something like
```
    # If the client connection failed or disconnect at any
    # point in the startup task we do not want
    # the exception to be raised here because it will
    # prevent the config entry from being unloaded.
    try:
        await start_client_task
    except NotConnected as ex:
        LOGGER.debug("Not connected to server: %s", ex)
    except BaseZwaveJSServerError as ex:
        LOGGER.exception("Error during disconnect: %s", ex)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
```

It looks like this would normally be rare since most users are using the addon locally and there is no network involved.  As soon as the connection happens over the network, I expect the failure rate would go up significantly so `NotConnected` could happen because something on the network had a hiccup as well.

I think the most likely case is the connection being closed out before the startup task is cancelled (which this PR should fix) but the above is also likely to happen as soon as its going across the network

The plan has been to refactor the integration to handle the setup similar to the matter integration. That will enable us to remove the start client task. Maybe we should just do that now to make everything simpler?
